history.new: Our own check covers n <= 2e5 (maximum 11 from n <= 1.25e4 on); the Skeptic's bitset computation to 1e6 also gives maximum 11 (P-density 0.1639 at 1e6, still rising).
history.old: Our own check covers n <= 2e5 only (maximum 11 from n <= 1.25e4 on).

limitations: Our own check covers n <= 2e5 (maximum 11 from n <= 1.25e4 on); the Skeptic's bitset computation to 1e6 also gives maximum 11 (P-density 0.1639 at 1e6, still rising).
novelty_basis:
OEIS A014589 records a(n) <= 11 for n <= 32452842 (A. Huet, 2022) and for n <= 1e9 (B. Dobbelaere, 2024);
we found no proof of boundedness.
statement: The Grundy values of the subtraction game whose move set is the set of primes satisfy g(n) <= 11 for all n.
title: Subtract-a-prime has Grundy values at most 11
